summary: Dispatched the case built to separate the sweep's two candidate conditions, after a local run that already changes how I read the confound. The case polls the origin's decided index for up to thirty seconds before re-electing it, so a completed re-synchronisation would be visible; locally it never completed — `resync_completed_before_reelection` false after a 30.1 s wait, the origin's decided index still 0 — and the shift was still delivered (`resolved` ok with index 3 while entry 33 sits at index 1 and the decided log is 33,34,35). That corrects my previous reading: `decided_after_resync` is not a proxy for the ordering between re-synchronisation and re-election at this construction, since it never flips regardless of waiting, so the sweep's apparent confound was a misreading on my side rather than a second live condition — which restores the tick period as the better-supported condition while leaving the stale placeholders' exact origin unobserved. The submitted case is a revision of the sweep experiment (the harness gained the poll flag and the wait/completion fields; existing cases unchanged) with one comparison asserting the returned index must be the entry's true position, locally violated. Incomplete: that receipt is pending, and why the origin's decided index never advances in this scenario remains open. No execution was requested beyond this one.
